install -r requirements.txt` if\\\\\\\\n+it is not already available. Start the foreground server with a port, for example:\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+```sh\\\\\\\\n+PORT=8000 ./run.sh\\\\\\\\n+```\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+The server binds only to `127.0.0.1`. In a separate shell, verify it with\\\\\\\\n+`curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health`; the response is `{\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"ok\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\":true}`. Do not run\\\\\\\\n+the server as part of static checks: `python3 -m py_compile app.py` verifies that\\\\\\\\n+the application imports successfully.\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+## Entry point and layout\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+`run.sh` sets the local dependency path and launches `app.py`. `app.py` is the\\\\\\\\n+single Flask application module. It contains the route registrations, small\\\\\\\\n+domain helpers, and SQLite access functions together so the API remains easy to\\\\\\\\n+audit. `requirements.txt` pins Flask 3.1.3. Generated reports and historical\\\\\\\\n+`shots/` directories record earlier benchmark runs; they are not application\\\\\\\\n+code.\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+## State and routing\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+Importing `app.py` creates `game.db` beside the module and idempotently creates\\\\\\\\n+the schema. `database_connection()` opens a new SQLite connection per operation,\\\\\\\\n+enables foreign keys, and uses context managers to commit successful writes or\\\\\\\\n+roll back failures. Combat session state is stored as compact JSON; users,\\\\\\\\n+compendium entries, campaigns, characters, and events are normalized tables.\\\\\\\\n+The storage status and reset routes expose the schema lifecycle.\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+Routes are grouped in source order by storage/authentication, campaigns,\\\\\\\\n+compendium, general dice and ability tools, DM encounter/loot/recap tools,\\\\\\\\n+combat sessions, character calculations, and PHB rules. Each route owns its\\\\\\\\n+public validation message and status code. Shared helpers only handle mechanical\\\\\\\\n+work such as parsing required JSON fields, nonblank text checks, initiative and\\\\\\\\n+encounter calculations, and database reads/writes.\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+## Safe extension and testing conventions\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+Treat route paths, JSON shape, error text, status codes, ordering, and SQLite\\\\\\\\n+persistence as API contract. Preserve strict `type(value) is int` checks where\\\\\\\\n+they are used: accepting booleans as integers would change validation behavior.\\\\\\\\n+Use parameterized SQL, retain explicit `ORDER BY position` for persisted ordered\\\\\\\\n+collections, and keep deterministic results (no random values or clock-based\\\\\\\\n+data). Add narrowly scoped helpers only when they do not choose route-specific\\\\\\\\n+errors or validation policy.\\\\\\\\n+\\\\\\\\n+Before changing behavior, run the available evaluator suite for the relevant\\\\\\\\n+feature. For refactoring-only work, at minimum run `python3 -m py_compile app.py`\\\\\\\\n+and inspect the diff; use `PORT=<port> ./run.sh` only when manual HTTP verification\\\\\\\\n+is needed.\\\\\\\\n?? Start the foreground server with a port, for example:\\\\n\\\\n```sh\\\\nPORT=8000 ./run.sh\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nThe server binds only to `127.0.0.1`. In a separate shell, verify it with\\\\n`curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health`; the response is `{\\\\\\\"ok\\\\\\\":true}`. Do not run\\\\nthe server as part of static checks: `python3 -m py_compile app.py` verifies that\\\\nthe application imports successfully.\\\\n\\\\n## Entry point and layout\\\\n\\\\n`run.sh` sets the local dependency path and launches `app.py`. `app.py` is the\\\\nsingle Flask application module. It contains the route registrations, small\\\\ndomain helpers, and SQLite access functions together so the API remains easy to\\\\naudit. `requirements.txt` pins Flask 3.1.3. Generated reports and historical\\\\n`shots/` directories record earlier benchmark runs; they are not application\\\\ncode.\\\\n\\\\n## State and routing\\\\n\\\\nImporting `app.py` creates `game.db` beside the module and idempotently creates\\\\nthe schema. `database_connection()` opens a new SQLite connection per operation,\\\\nenables foreign keys, and uses context managers to commit successful writes or\\\\nroll back failures. Combat session state is stored as compact JSON; users,\\\\ncompendium entries, campaigns, characters, and events are normalized tables.\\\\nThe storage status and reset routes expose the schema lifecycle.\\\\n\\\\nRoutes are grouped in source order by storage/authentication, campaigns,\\\\ncompendium, general dice and ability tools, DM encounter/loot/recap tools,\\\\ncombat sessions, character calculations, and PHB rules. Each route owns its\\\\npublic validation message and status code. Shared helpers only handle mechanical\\\\nwork such as parsing required JSON fields, nonblank text checks, initiative and\\\\nencounter calculations, and database reads/writes.\\\\n\\\\n## Safe extension and testing conventions\\\\n\\\\nTreat route paths, JSON shape, error text, status codes, ordering, and SQLite\\\\npersistence as API contract. Preserve strict `type(value) is int` checks where\\\\nthey are used: accepting booleans as integers would change validation behavior.\\\\nUse parameterized SQL, retain explicit `ORDER BY position` for persisted ordered\\\\ncollections, and keep deterministic results (no random values or clock-based\\\\ndata). Add narrowly scoped helpers only when they do not choose route-specific\\\\nerrors or validation policy.\\\\n\\\\nBefore changing behavior, run the available evaluator suite for the relevant\\\\nfeature.
